definitions.doc_after:
Wrap a named Colossus cosmology while restoring global state after calls.

Parameters
----------
name : str
    Named Colossus cosmology, such as planck18, used for every background query.

Notes
-----
The default planck18 preset is supplied by Colossus and is based on Planck 2018. The
preset is external library data; its full parameter set is not inferred from the rounded
native defaults.

Each query activates the named Colossus cosmology and restores the previous global
selection. The wrapper preserves the implemented provider conversion; comparisons must
also check factors of h, not only matching parameter labels.

References
----------

.. [cite-colossus] Diemer (2018), COLOSSUS: A Python Toolkit for Cosmology, Large-scale Structure, and Dark Matter Halos.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04512

.. [cite-planck] Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209

Return 1.686 divided by the growth factor.

Parameters
----------
z : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.

Returns
-------
float or numpy.ndarray
    Dimensionless linearly extrapolated spherical-collapse barrier 1.686/D(z).

Notes
-----
The adopted spherical-collapse barrier is delta_c(z)=1.686/D(z), as used in Ludlow et
al., Appendix C. This approximation is separate from any mass-dependent WDM collapse
correction.

definitions.doc_after:
Flat-LCDM background with NumPy/SciPy only.

Parameters
----------
omega_m0
    Present-day matter density fraction.
h
    Reduced Hubble constant.

Notes
-----
The defaults Omega_m0=0.315 and h=0.674 are rounded Planck-2018 values. User-supplied
alternatives remain explicit background choices.

This matter-plus-Lambda, spatially flat background neglects radiation. Growth uses the
Carroll-Press-Turner approximation normalized to D(0)=1; the generic background is not a
calibration of a SASHIMI halo prescription.

References
----------

.. [cite-planck] Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209

definitions.doc_after:
Return the Carroll-Press-Turner growth approximation normalized at z=0.

Parameters
----------
z : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.

Returns
-------
float or numpy.ndarray
    Dimensionless linear growth D(z), normalized at z=0.

Notes
-----
The factors 5/2, 4/7 and 1/70 belong to the Carroll--Press--Turner growth approximation.
Redshift derivatives differentiate that approximation; they are not a separate growth
calibration.

This matter-plus-Lambda, spatially flat background neglects radiation. Growth uses the
Carroll-Press-Turner approximation normalized to D(0)=1; the generic background is not a
calibration of a SASHIMI halo prescription.

References
----------

.. [cite-growth] Carroll, Press & Turner (1992), The Cosmological Constant, Section 3.5, Eq. (29).
    https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.aa.30.090192.002435
    Full text: https://ned.ipac.caltech.edu/level5/Carroll/Carroll3_5.html

definitions.doc_after:
Return ``ln(1+x)-x/(1+x)`` for finite nonnegative ``x``.

A small-radius series avoids subtracting two nearly equal terms. Values
smaller than the floating-point subnormal range can still underflow.

Parameters
----------
x : float or array_like
    Nonnegative dimensionless NFW radius r/r_s; zero gives zero enclosed mass.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    Dimensionless f(x)=ln(1+x)-x/(1+x), retaining the nonnegative radius-ratio shape.

Notes
-----
The enclosed-mass factor ln(1+c)-c/(1+c) follows the NFW density profile. Algebraic
inversion tolerances concern this profile identity, not agreement with simulated halos.

The enclosed-mass normalization is M(<r)=4*pi*rho_s*r_s**3*f(r/r_s). The potential fixes
G in Mpc*(km/s)^2/Msun and its zero at infinity, so use Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3 for physical
profile parameters.

References
----------

.. [cite-nfw] Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9611107

definitions.doc_after:
Invert the NFW enclosed-mass function over representable positive radii.

Solve in log-radius so an absolute tolerance in radius cannot erase a
small, positive solution. The output retains the input shape.

Parameters
----------
y : float or array_like
    Dimensionless enclosed mass M/(4*pi*rho_s*r_s**3), within the representable inverse
    range.

Returns
-------
float or numpy.ndarray
    Nonnegative radius ratio r/r_s whose NFW mass function equals y; input shape is
    retained.

Notes
-----
The enclosed-mass factor ln(1+c)-c/(1+c) follows the NFW density profile. Algebraic
inversion tolerances concern this profile identity, not agreement with simulated halos.

The enclosed-mass normalization is M(<r)=4*pi*rho_s*r_s**3*f(r/r_s). The potential fixes
G in Mpc*(km/s)^2/Msun and its zero at infinity, so use Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3 for physical
profile parameters.

Navarro et al. print the density and circular-speed relations. The potential with zero
at infinity and numerical or Lambert-W inversion of the enclosed-mass factor are
derived consequences of that profile; these closed forms and solver controls are not
equations printed in the cited paper.

References
----------

.. [cite-nfw] Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9611107

definitions.doc_after:
Detect gross background mismatches against the optional Colossus implementation.

Notes
-----
Planck-like background numbers are controlled test inputs. Equality or rejection here
checks the stated background contract, not the cosmological fit.

Pass criteria: At z=0,1,3 the two Planck-like backgrounds agree within 3 percent in H
and 4 percent in growth.

Failure criteria: any mismatch with the stated value, shape or identity requirements
fails the test.

Scope: Only H and growth are compared, not critical/matter density. The current Colossus
wrapper multiplies its Msun*h^2/kpc^3 density by 1e9 without applying h^2; this test
cannot detect that canonical-unit mismatch.

References
----------

.. [cite-planck] Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209

definitions.doc_after:
Avoid cache aliasing between numerically distinct cosmological parameters.

Notes
-----
Planck-like background numbers are controlled test inputs. Equality or rejection here
checks the stated background contract, not the cosmological fit.

Pass criteria: h=0.674 and h=0.67400000001 produce different identifiers.

Failure criteria: any mismatch with the stated value, shape or identity requirements
fails the test.

Scope: This controlled calculation does not calibrate a subhalo population against
simulations or observations.

References
----------

.. [cite-planck] Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209

planck.title: Planck Collaboration (2020), Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters, Table 2.
planck.manual_comparison: H0=67.36, Omega_m=0.3153, omega_b=0.02237, tau=0.0544 and A_s=2.100e-9 support the rounded native/control inputs. Omega_b is obtained by dividing omega_b by h^2. The Colossus planck18 preset selects a different data combination; its name does not make it identical to the native parameter vector.

colossus.title: Diemer (2018), COLOSSUS: A Python Toolkit for Cosmology, Large-scale Structure, and Dark Matter Halos.
colossus.manual_comparison: The v3 paper lists planck18 (H0=67.66, Omega_m=0.3111, Omega_b=0.0490) and planck18-only (67.36, 0.3153, 0.0493) separately. It describes named presets and global cosmology state. Saving/restoring that state is this wrapper's implementation, not a published physical equation.

growth.title: Carroll, Press & Turner (1992), The Cosmological Constant, Section 3.5.
growth.manual_comparison: The displayed growth suppression is g=2.5*Omega_m/[Omega_m^(4/7)-Omega_Lambda+(1+Omega_m/2)*(1+Omega_Lambda/70)]. The normalized D(z)=g(z)/[(1+z)*g(0)] and code redshift derivatives are derived uses. The DOI reaches a publisher landing page; the NED equation image provides accessible full text.

ludlow.title: Ludlow et al. (2016), The mass-concentration-redshift relation of cold and warm dark matter haloes, Appendix C.
ludlow.location: Eq. (3) and following text, p.5; Appendix C, pp.18-19, Eqs. (C8)-(C12)
ludlow.manual_comparison: The paper explicitly uses delta_sc(z)=1.686/D(z). The variance fit is sigma=22.26*xi^0.292/(1+1.53*xi^0.275+3.36*xi^0.198), xi=(M/(1e10 h^-1 Msun))^-1. It reports about 2.5% fit accuracy over 1e-7 to 1e15 h^-1 Msun. Differentiation is derived. WDM host histories integrate their spectrum and do not use this CDM variance fit; their redundant citation was removed.

nfw.title: Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
nfw.manual_comparison: The density and circular-speed laws are printed. f(x)=ln(1+x)-x/(1+x) follows by integrating the density. Potential with zero at infinity, exact mass-conversion root finding, and c=-1/W0(-exp[-(y+1)])-1 are derived consequences; the paper does not print the implementation's inverse or solver. The 2.163 and 4.625 factors are rounded maximum-speed identities.
